about: The decorator contract table (research 2026-10-27, section 1): a framework decorator, keyed by package and export, with its wrapper relation in a closed vocabulary, so that lean models the boundary and never the framework. Lane A reads a listed decorator as its row says (a guard gates the body, a pipe transforms a parameter, a metadata API reads or writes a cell of the world keyed by (key, target)); lane B applies the same row in its fakes. A row is trusted only for its framework version; a row whose fixture disagrees with the real framework is a defect of the table and the proof lane withholds every reading that used it (ASK:decorator-model). A decorator outside the table keeps today's reading: text in the signature.

vocabulary.kind: route | guard | pipe | inject | metadata | marker
vocabulary.target: class | method | parameter | property, the places the decorator is written
vocabulary.body: unchanged: the decorated method runs as written (no listed decorator replaces it)
vocabulary.guard: the call runs only when every guard answers true; class guards run first, then method guards, each in argument order; a false answer throws before the body
vocabulary.pipe: the parameter value is the result of each pipe argument in order, applied to the value the framework extracted; a leading string argument names the extracted property and is no pipe
vocabulary.inject: the parameter or field is the provider the container resolves for the token (else for the declared type), read once at construction
vocabulary.metadata: the cells the decorator writes at class definition, or the cell an API reads or writes at run time: a cell is keyed by (key, target) where the target is the class or the handler function
vocabulary.errors: what the relation may throw, by the framework's own exception class
vocabulary.effects: what the decorator records or asks of the world
vocabulary.framework: the package the row is about
vocabulary.version: the framework version range the row is trusted for
vocabulary.fixture: the harness fixture that runs the decorator through the installed framework and checks the row's claim; status agree | disagree | pending
